chunks: Al-Husayn ibn Muhammad, from Mu'alla ibn Muhammad, from Al-Hasan ibn Ali, from Aban ibn Uthman, from the one who narrated it, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) regarding
a man who borrowed a garment, then he took it and mortgaged it. Then the owners of the goods came to their goods. He (peace be upon him) said: 'They take their goods.'

key_terms.رَهَنَهُ: mortgaged it / pledged it as collateral
key_terms.يَأْخُذُونَ: they take / they have the right to take

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling on a borrowed item that the borrower mortgages to someone else?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Kafi clarifies the principle of 'gharar' (uncertainty) in transactions by establishing that a borrower who pledges a borrowed item without the owner's consent does not transfer full ownership rights to the creditor. Consequently, the original owner retains the right to reclaim their property directly, prioritizing the security of the principal asset over the creditor's claim. This ruling underscores the Shia jurisprudential emphasis on preserving the rights of the original owner in cases of unauthorized disposal or pledging.

en.hubeali:
Al Husayn Bin Muhammad, from Moalla Bin Muhammad, from Al Hassan Bin Ali, from Aban Bin Usman, from the one who narrated it, 
(It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> regarding
a man who borrowed clothes, then he deliberated to it so he mortgaged it. Then the rightful owners of the goods cam to their goods’. He<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘They can take their goods’.
en.sarwar: 6. Al-Husayn from Muhammad has narrated from Mu’alla’ ibn Muhammad from al-Hassan ibn Ali from Aban ibn ‘Uthman from the one who narrated to him who has said the following: “This is concerning my question before abu ‘Abd Allah, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, about
the case of a man who borrowed clothes, then left it as al-Rahn (security deposit) with someone; then the owner came to take it. He (the Imam) said, ‘They can take their asset.’”
